Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a concise Helio Start decision evidence card for the March 2024 public-product decision. Summarize the readiness cohort evidence across operating volume, support coverage, state integrity, excluded operational cases, and the limits on what the evidence justified. Make the distinction between what the cohort established and what it did not establish explicit. Create it as a new document in the Growth folder.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Helio Start — March 2024 public-product decision evidence card", "folder": "Growth", "body": "Helio Start — March 2024 public-product decision evidence card

Decision context
The capped readiness cohort supported a bounded public-product decision under the existing eligibility, refusal, and assisted-routing rules. It did not support broad or unrestricted availability.

Cohort and cutoff
- 120 applications reviewed from the controlled cohort; the results used the February 23, 2024, 5:00 PM Central cutoff.
- 104 accounts were admitted: 76 exact-match admin proofs and 28 legitimate mismatches accepted with corroborating admin evidence.
- 16 applications were routed out for agency identity, unresolved ownership, manual billing, import, or migration needs.

Evidence established

Operating volume
- 82 of the 104 admitted accounts created workspaces.
- 68 reached first integration by day 7.
- Workspace creation and first integration were treated as separate operating checkpoints, not as a single success measure.

Support coverage
- Customer Success handled 9 ordinary setup questions and 4 permissions or ownership reviews within normal coverage.
- The observed support load was compatible with the bounded operating model, with assisted cases remaining visible rather than being absorbed into self-serve outcomes.

State integrity
- Daniela’s audit showed one current entitlement state and one current support state for every admitted workspace.
- This made the admitted-path activation and support readout interpretable within the reviewed cohort.

Excluded operational cases
- The 16 routed applications stayed outside the admitted self-serve path.
- No manual-billing, import, or migration case entered the admitted path.
- Agency identity and unresolved ownership remained routing or refusal conditions; corroborating evidence was permitted only for legitimate domain mismatches.

What the cohort justified
- A bounded public self-serve path, later approved for March 18, limited to accounts meeting the stated eligibility and supported-operating conditions.
- Continued first-class measurement of activation, support load, entitlement state, support state, and routing quality.
- Preservation of the refusal and assisted-routing boundaries.

What the cohort did not establish
- It did not establish unrestricted GA, broad eligibility, or that seat count alone qualifies an account.
- It did not establish demand, acquisition efficiency, forecastable pipeline, predictable revenue, or a basis for paid acquisition.
- It did not prove that the product or admin path was solved for all cases, or that routed cases were activation failures.
- It did not justify admitting agency, unresolved-ownership, manual-billing, import, migration, or unsupported-permission cases into ordinary self-serve.
- It did not justify merging Helio Start results with retained mid-segment or Expansion Assist evidence.

Decision-safe conclusion
The cohort demonstrated bounded operating capacity for the eligible, supported case—not a general market, revenue, or unrestricted-launch claim. The March decision was therefore valid only with the existing rules, routing boundaries, separate denominators, and ongoing support/state-integrity monitoring."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_057_02", "path": "args", "criterion": "The document states that the readiness cohort covered 120 applications and explains that eligible accounts demonstrated activation at higher operating volume. The document states that no manual-billing, import, or migration case entered the admitted path. All three excluded case types must be represented.

The document clearly concludes that the cohort supported a bounded GA or bounded public-product decision, but did not justify unrestricted admission or removal of the existing refusal boundaries. Decision context
The capped readiness cohort supported a bounded public-product decision under the existing eligibility, refusal, and assisted-routing rules. It did not support broad or unrestricted availability.

Cohort and cutoff
- 120 applications reviewed from the controlled cohort; the results used the February 23, 2024, 5:00 PM Central cutoff.
- 104 accounts were admitted: 76 exact-match admin proofs and 28 legitimate mismatches accepted with corroborating admin evidence.
- 16 applications were routed out for agency identity, unresolved ownership, manual billing, import, or migration needs.

Evidence established

Operating volume
- 82 of the 104 admitted accounts created workspaces.
- 68 reached first integration by day 7.
- Workspace creation and first integration were treated as separate operating checkpoints, not as a single success measure.

Support coverage
- Customer Success handled 9 ordinary setup questions and 4 permissions or ownership reviews within normal coverage.
- The observed support load was compatible with the bounded operating model, with assisted cases remaining visible rather than being absorbed into self-serve outcomes.

State integrity
- Daniela’s audit showed one current entitlement state and one current support state for every admitted workspace.
- This made the admitted-path activation and support readout interpretable within the reviewed cohort.

Excluded operational cases
- The 16 routed applications stayed outside the admitted self-serve path.
- No manual-billing, import, or migration case entered the admitted path.
- Agency identity and unresolved ownership remained routing or refusal conditions; corroborating evidence was permitted only for legitimate domain mismatches.

What the cohort justified
- A bounded public self-serve path, later approved for March 18, limited to accounts meeting the stated eligibility and supported-operating conditions.
- Continued first-class measurement of activation, support load, entitlement state, support state, and routing quality.
- Preservation of the refusal and assisted-routing boundaries.

What the cohort did not establish
- It did not establish unrestricted GA, broad eligibility, or that seat count alone qualifies an account.
- It did not establish demand, acquisition efficiency, forecastable pipeline, predictable revenue, or a basis for paid acquisition.
- It did not prove that the product or admin path was solved for all cases, or that routed cases were activation failures.
- It did not justify admitting agency, unresolved-ownership, manual-billing, import, migration, or unsupported-permission cases into ordinary self-serve.
- It did not justify merging Helio Start results with retained mid-segment or Expansion Assist evidence.

Decision-safe conclusion
The cohort demonstrated bounded operating capacity for the eligible, supported case—not a general market, revenue, or unrestricted-launch claim. The March decision was therefore valid only with the existing rules, routing boundaries, separate denominators, and ongoing support/state-integrity monitoring."}}]}
